paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take from Psalm 55, friend. David doesn't clean up his prayer before he brings it. His heart pounds, he wants to run off like a dove, and he even says some pretty fierce things about the people who hurt him (Psalm 55:4, 6, 15). And God lets him say ALL of it. That tells me you can bring Him the messy version, the 3 a.m. version, the version with no polite words in it.

Then look at what hurts David most. It isn't an enemy, it's a companion and close friend, someone he walked with into the house of God (Psalm 55:12-14). If somebody close to you has turned on you, this psalm says you are not being dramatic and you are not alone. David doesn't hide the pain, and he doesn't stay stuck in it either. He says, "But I call to God, and the LORD saves me" (Psalm 55:16).

So what do we do with the weight? David says, "Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken" (Psalm 55:22). Notice he doesn't say the burden disappears first, he says to throw it on the One strong enough to carry it. And he ends the whole psalm with a choice: "But I will trust in You" (Psalm 55:23). Baker, you don't have to grow wings and fly away. Cast it, trust Him, and let Him hold what you can't.
